candidates.title: moveLiquidity Fraxswap migration is manipulable: attacker pre-creates/skews the Fraxswap pair, the permissionless migration's alignment swaps + final mint (no slippage) execute at attacker terms -> value theft
candidates.description: moveLiquidity() is permissionless once the CCY end-criterion is met. If the Fraxswap pair already exists (an attacker can createPair + seed a skewed reserve beforehand), addLiquidityToFraxswap does a mini-mint + 3 approximate alignment swaps + a final mint, all with NO slippage/minOut bounds, against the attacker-controlled pair. The attacker sandwiches the alignment swaps / captures the mispriced LP, stealing migrated value; leftover tokens are then swept to the agent. RULE: migration must be atomic/slippage-bounded, reject or neutralize a pre-existing skewed pair, and not perform unbounded alignment swaps against external reserves.

candidates.title: moveLiquidity sizes the Fraxswap add using the bootstrap pool SPOT price -> manipulable just before migration
candidates.description: price = bootstrapPool.getPrice() (spot from reserves incl phantomAmount); liquidityAmount = currencyAmount*1e18/price. A large buy/sell on the (permissionless) bootstrap pool right before the (permissionless) moveLiquidity skews the spot price, so the migration adds liquidity at a wrong ratio and the leftover tokens (swept to agent) leak value. RULE: use a manipulation-resistant price (TWAP) or enforce min-LP/ratio bounds on the migration add.

candidates.title: TokenGovernor.setProposalThresholdPercentage validates the OLD storage var instead of the new parameter -> can set threshold above the 10% max
candidates.description: `if (proposalThresholdPercentage > 1000) revert InvalidThreshold();` checks the CURRENT (old) `proposalThresholdPercentage`, then assigns `proposalThresholdPercentage = _proposalThresholdPercentage`. The bound is applied to the wrong variable — the NEW value `_proposalThresholdPercentage` is never validated, so governance can set it >1000 (>10%), e.g. to a value that makes proposals impossible (DoS governance) or trivially low. RULE: validate the incoming parameter, not the existing storage. Anchor: a setter that `require`s on the state var it is about to overwrite instead of the argument.

candidates.title: BootstrapPool.buy/sell (and createAgent initial buy) have no slippage param -> sandwich when called directly (bypassing AgentRouter)
candidates.description: BootstrapPool.buy(_amountIn)/sell(_amountIn) are public with NO minAmountOut; only AgentRouter adds _minAmountOut. Users/integrators calling the pool directly (and AgentFactory.createAgent's `_amountToBuy` initial buy) get sandwiched on the bonding curve. RULE: enforce minOut at the pool level too, or document the router as the only safe entry. (Lift-test: matches the reincorporated missing-slippage pattern.)

candidates.title: BootstrapPool.buy doesn't assert agentToken balance >= agentTokenFeeEarned (sell asserts the currency side) -> asymmetric fee-backing
candidates.description: sell() ends with require(currencyToken.balanceOf >= currencyTokenFeeEarned) but buy() has no symmetric require(agentToken.balanceOf >= agentTokenFeeEarned). Edge accounting/availability inconsistency for the agent-side fee. Low.
